newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Feb 13.

text.p: There are 138 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- EXPRESS NEWS said that the decision that British expatriates would have to apply for visas to remain in the territory reflected the sovereignty of China after the handover, because the British would become foreigners in Hong Kong. It said people who had made special contributions to Hong Kong should be allowed to stay regardless of their nationality.

-- TA KUNG PAO said that the meeting between British and Chinese foreign ministers on Friday might be the last before the handover and the British election. It would be good for both sides for Britain to cooperate with China. It said it would be a waste of time for the British side to repeat its stance on issues such as the provisional legislature and amending present Hong Kong laws.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD said that with only five months of British rule left, it might be prudent to leave the issue of the establishment of a Central Provident Fund for Hong Kong workers to the SAR government. A fuller debate on a CPF rather than to rely extensively on the arguments of fund managers, might serve Hong Kong's interests best.
